Original model and complete seed hypothesis\n\nFor a nonnegative integer n and a nonnegative schedule\nh=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), define W_n(h) to be the supremum of\n\n    2(f(x_n)-f(x_star))/(L ||x_0-x_star||^2)\n\nover every finite-dimensional Euclidean space, every convex differentiable\nfunction f with L-Lipschitz gradient and at least one minimizer x_star,\nand every x_0!=x_star, under\n\n    x_(i+1)=x_i-(h_i/L) grad f(x_i).\n\nHere L>0 is fixed but arbitrary. This is the original W=2R normalization;\nthe empty schedule is included.\n\nFor nonnegative a,d set\n\n    Omega(a,d)=(a+d+sqrt((a+d)^2+4ad))/2,\n    G(a,d)=2a+d/2+sqrt(d^2+8ad)/2.\n\nRetain all original integer splits:\n\n    C_0=B_0=1,\n    C_n=max_(0<=k<n) Omega(C_k,C_(n-k-1)),\n    B_n=max_(0<=k<n) G(C_k,B_(n-k-1)),      n>=1.\n\nWrite U_n^ZJ=1/B_n, lambda=1+sqrt(2), and rho=log_2(lambda).\n\nFix an integer r>=1. A seed in this draft means an ACTUAL word\nh=(h_0,...,h_(r-1)) with every h_i>=0, sum s, capacity A=1+s,\nand m=r+1, together with a full real (r+1)-by-(r+1) array Lambda.\nFor EVERY ordered distinct pair i,j in {0,...,r}, require\n\n    Lambda_ij>=0,     Lambda_ii=0.\n\nLet e be the all-ones column of length r+1, and define\n\n    T_ii=1,  T_it=h_t for t<i,  T_it=0 for t>i,\n    L_flow=diag(Lambda e)-Lambda,\n    omega=(-2h_0,...,-2h_(r-1),2s)^T,\n    D_prim=diag(h_0(2-h_0),...,h_(r-1)(2-h_(r-1)),-s(s+2)).\n\nThe full original-coordinate certificate requirements are\n\n    L_flow^T e=omega,\n    M_prim=D_prim+(L_flow T+T^T L_flow^T)/2 >=0 on R^(r+1).       (1)\n\nTranspose and positive semidefiniteness have their ordinary real-matrix\nmeanings. There are exactly r(r+1) off-diagonal multipliers. Every formal\ngradient g_0,...,g_r remains, even when physical steps vanish. No gradient\nequality or coordinate deletion is allowed at a zero step. There is no\nassumption h_i>=1, product balance, zero remainder, rank, support, or\nsymmetry. These are precisely the general-length sufficient hypotheses\nin accepted `04219554e41d9750`, proof Section 10.\n\nFor clarity about their scope, that accepted result normalizes L=1 and\nuses x_i=x_0-sum_(t<i) h_t g_t and\n\n    Q_ij=f_i-f_j+<g_i,x_j-x_i>+||g_i-g_j||^2/2,\n    V_h=2sum_(i<r)h_i(f_i-f_r)\n        +sum_(i<r)h_i(1-h_i)||g_i||^2-s(s+1)||g_r||^2.\n\nIts exact identity is\n\n    V_h+sum_(i!=j) Lambda_ij Q_ij\n       =<M_prim,Gram(g_0,...,g_r)>.\n\nActual smooth convex trajectories have Q_ij<=0. Thus (1) implies the\nprimitive inequality on the full function class. Here Gram is the matrix\nof pairwise inner products, and the matrix pairing is trace(M^T Gram).\nThis accepted implication is only sufficiency; no attainment or equivalence\nof certificate classes is assumed.\n\n## 2. Accepted ray and physical-substitution inputs\n\nThe following are precise statements used from `04219554e41d9750`.\nFor every positive integer b, the limit\n\n    Z_b=lim_(j->infinity) lambda^(-j) B_(b*2^j-1)\n\nexists and is finite and positive. For every integer j>=0 put\n\n    L_pc(b,j)=lambda^(-j) B_(b*2^j-1),\n    U_pc(b,j)=lambda^(-j)(sqrt(B_(b*2^j))+3/100)^2,\n\n    E(b,j)=8sqrt(2)b^(rho-1)2^(-j)\n           +(3/25)(b+1)^(rho/2)lambda^(-j/2)\n           +(9/10000)lambda^(-j).\n\nThe accepted enclosures and their proof give\n\n    L_pc(b,j)<=Z_b<=U_pc(b,j),\n    0<=U_pc(b,j)-L_pc(b,j)<=E(b,j).                         (2)\n\nIndeed the latter is exactly the bound obtained by subtracting the two\nendpoints in accepted Section 9: use the accepted adjacent bound for\nB_(b*2^j)-B_(b*2^j-1) and B_n<=4C_n<=4(n+1)^rho. In particular both\nendpoints tend to Z_b. For every fixed integer d>=0 and defined index,\n\n    0<=Z_b-lambda^(-j)B_(b*2^j-1-d)\n       <=E(b,j)+8sqrt(2)d b^(rho-1)2^(-j).                  (3)\n\nThe same accepted proof gives\n\n    1<rho<4/3,\n    B_n>=C_n,\n    C_(b*2^j-1)=lambda^j C_(b-1),\n    C_(b-1)>=1.                                           (4)\n\nFor every nonnegative n, take any fully expanded maximizing tree of the\nORIGINAL B_n recurrence, expanding every primitive child using the\nORIGINAL C recurrence. Such a tree has n internal nodes, n primitive\nempty leaves, and one terminal dominant empty leaf. In particular,\nthere is no restriction on a maximizing dominant split.\n\nReplace each primitive empty leaf by the actual seed of Section 1.\nRetain all internal nodes and keep the dominant empty leaf empty with\nmass 1. Recompute all physical bridges:\n\n* At a primitive join, for actual child capacities A_left,A_right, use\n  bridge 1+d_pp, where d_pp>0 solves\n  d_pp(A_left+A_right+d_pp)=A_left A_right.\n* At a dominant join, for primitive left capacity A_left and actual\n  dominant right mass D_right=1+2sum(right), use bridge\n  1+A_left/zeta, where zeta=(1+sqrt(1+8A_left/D_right))/2.\n\nConcatenate (left,bridge,right) at every node. Denote the resulting word\nby Hsub_n, and its ACTUAL mass by Dsub_n=1+2sum Hsub_n. Accepted\nSections 11--12 apply for every seed satisfying (1), including arbitrary\nPSD remainders and zero steps. They give\n\n    length(Hsub_n)=mn,\n    W_(mn)(Hsub_n)=1/Dsub_n,\n    (sqrt(A B_n)-(sqrt(A)-1))^2<=Dsub_n<=A B_n.             (5)\n\nThe upper objective certificate holds for all functions in Section 1;\nits matching Huber example gives the displayed equality. In particular\nthis is not merely a quadratic or projection-family assertion.\n\nThe length in (5) counts n old bridge steps and nr seed steps. The lower\nmass bound pays for the one untouched dominant leaf: all primitive\ncapacities scale by A, while the square-root dominant merge is\n1-Lipschitz in the square root of the right mass. This is why the\nsubtraction sqrt(A)-1 is present. We never physically replace the\ndominant empty leaf by an object of mass A.\n\n## 3. Integer-ray monotonicity and exact dyadic scaling\n\nThe admissible split k=0 in B_(n+1) gives\n\n    B_(n+1)>=G(1,B_n)>B_n,\n\nbecause B_n>0 and sqrt(B_n^2+8B_n)>B_n. Thus B is increasing directly\nfrom the ORIGINAL recurrence. If positive integers b<=c, then\n\n    B_(b*2^j-1)<=B_(c*2^j-1)\n\nfor every j. Taking the established limits proves Z_b<=Z_c. We do not\nneed or assert strict increase of the ray limits.\n\nFor every integer ell>=0, changing the limiting index gives\n\n    Z_(2^ell b)\n      =lim_j lambda^(-j)B_(b*2^(j+ell)-1)\n      =lambda^ell Z_b.                                    (6)\n\nThis uses the accepted integer-ray limits only. No continuity, density,\nor regularity of a real-valued phase function has been assumed.\n\n## 4. The finite product and its strict margin\n\nChoose positive integers b0,d,K and an integer ell>=0. Let C_pc be a\npositive certified upper bound for Z_d/Z_b0. Suppose\n\n    m^K b0<=2^ell d.\n\nDefine, for 0<=i<=K,\n\n    b_i=b0 m^i,\n    P_pc=lambda^ell C_pc.\n\nAll quantities Z_b are positive. Exact telescoping, monotonicity, and\n(6), in that order, prove\n\n    product_(i=0)^(K-1) [Z_(m b_i)/Z_b_i]\n      =Z_(m^K b0)/Z_b0\n      <=Z_(2^ell d)/Z_b0\n      =lambda^ell Z_d/Z_b0\n      <=P_pc.                                             (7)\n\nEvery inequality has the direction required for an UPPER product bound.\nIn particular this argument never turns an upper ray enclosure into a\nlower bound for an unknown ratio.\n\nAlso m^K b0>=b0, so monotonicity makes the telescoped ratio at least 1.\nThus P_pc>=1, and the strict capacity condition A^K>P_pc implies A>1.\n\nIt is convenient to allow a certified capacity floor a with 1<a<=A.\nAssume a^K>P_pc and choose a positive gamma satisfying\n\n    K gamma<=1-P_pc/a^K.                                  (8)\n\nNecessarily gamma<1. Write\n\n    q_i(a)=Z_(m b_i)/(a Z_b_i).\n\nThe product of the q_i(a) is at most t_pc=P_pc/a^K<1. Therefore some\nindex i_star in {0,...,K-1} satisfies q_i_star(a)<=t_pc^(1/K).\nOtherwise their product would exceed t_pc.\n\nFor completeness, for x in [0,1] the inequality\n(1-x)^K>=1-Kx follows by induction: multiplying the induction bound by\n1-x adds the nonnegative term K x^2. With x=gamma, (8) gives\n\n    (1-gamma)^K>=1-K gamma>=t_pc.\n\nConsequently there is a fixed index i_star with\n\n    Z_(m b_i_star)/(A Z_b_i_star)\n      <=q_i_star(a)<=1-gamma.                             (9)\n\nThis is an existence assertion about a finite list, not a selection of\nan unproved optimal phase. Sections 5--6 make it a physical and certified\nstatement.\n\n## 5. Physical families, exact offsets, and uniform limit passage\n\nFor each i in {0,...,K-1} and integer j>=0, put\n\n    n_(i,j)=b_i 2^j-1,\n    N_(i,j)=m n_(i,j)=m b_i 2^j-m,\n    H_(i,j)=Hsub_(n_(i,j)).\n\nThus there are K explicitly defined schedule families. At a fixed j\nthere are exactly K specified finite physical words, possibly with\ndifferent lengths. Each word is generated by the procedure in Section 2,\nfor example with the least maximizing split used to resolve ties.\n\nThe numerator is evaluated at its TRUE physical horizon. Equation (3)\napplies with ray m b_i and shift d=m-1=r, since\n\n    N_(i,j)=m b_i 2^j-1-(m-1).\n\nIt proves lambda^(-j)B_(N_(i,j))->Z_(m b_i). Also (5) yields\n\n    0<=A Z_b_i-lambda^(-j)Dsub_(n_(i,j))\n      <=A E(b_i,j)\n        +2(sqrt(A)-1)sqrt(A Z_b_i)lambda^(-j/2).           (10)\n\nTo see the second term, subtract the square in (5) from A B_n,\ndiscard the negative term -(sqrt(A)-1)^2, and use\nB_(n_(i,j))<=lambda^j Z_b_i. Thus the denominator converges to\nA Z_b_i>0. By (5),\n\n    lim_j B_(N_(i,j)) W_(N_(i,j))(H_(i,j))\n        =Z_(m b_i)/(A Z_b_i).                             (11)\n\nThere are only K indices. In (3) use the maximum ray m b_(K-1) and\nthe fixed shift m-1; in (10) use b_(K-1) and Z_b_(K-1). These give\ncommon errors tending to zero, while every denominator limit is at least\nA because Z_b>=L_pc(b,0)=B_(b-1)>=1. Therefore (11) is uniform over\nthe finite list and over all maximizing-tree ties. No interchange of\nan infinite phase minimum with a limit is involved.\n\nFor any one fixed selected i, the integers N_(i,j) strictly increase\nand tend to infinity with j. The words at different horizons need not\nbe prefixes of one another; the original prescribed-horizon guarantee\ndoes not require that property.\n\n## 6. Certified phase selection and an explicit common horizon\n\nAt a search depth t>=0 compute, or supply certified enclosures for,\nthe K quantities\n\n    F_i(t)=U_pc(m b_i,t)/(a L_pc(b_i,t)).                   (12)\n\nThey are valid upper bounds on q_i(a): the numerator is bounded from\nabove and the positive denominator from below. Both endpoints in (2)\nconverge, so F_i(t)->q_i(a). Choose the first t for which some\n\n    F_i(t)<1-gamma/2,                                    (13)\n\nand freeze the smallest such i. This rule terminates: the index supplied\nby (9) has limit at most 1-gamma, leaving the strict slack gamma/2.\nIt is unnecessary to decide which index minimizes the true ray ratio.\n\nThis is a certified convergent procedure, not a prescription to use\nuncertified floating-point comparisons. For rational a and gamma, it has\nthe following finite-precision implementation in principle. At stage\nt>=1, form outward rational enclosures of each L_pc(b_i,t) and\nU_pc(m b_i,t) with absolute error at most 2^(-t), keeping every lower\ndenominator positive. Use the lower L endpoint and upper U endpoint\nin (12), and stop only upon the strict rational inequality (13).\nEach finite B value is defined by finitely many additions, products,\npositive square roots, and maxima in the ORIGINAL recurrence. These\noperations admit arbitrarily accurate rational outward enclosures:\nrational square comparisons bracket each positive square root, and the\nmaximum of lower or upper endpoints bounds the corresponding maximum.\nFor a fixed stage only finitely many such operations are needed. The\nrecurrences have positive inputs, so arbitrary prescribed absolute\naccuracy follows by refinement. The extra errors tend to zero with t,\nand termination follows from the same strict slack. There is no claim\nthat this procedure is computationally economical, and it was not run.\n\nMore generally, an arbitrary real seed need not come with a computable\ncapacity oracle. The effective input is a certified rational floor\n1<a<=A with a^K>P_pc, and a certified positive rational gamma satisfying\n(8). If A^K>P_pc, such choices exist by strictness and rational density;\ntheir certification uses the supplied seed data. This states the actual\ninput required for effective selection rather than presuming an oracle\nfor arbitrary real numbers. The exact-real formulation (12)--(13) is\nalso a valid mathematical selection rule.\n\nIt remains to turn the selected ratio into a bound for every sufficiently\nlarge physical horizon. Put b_max=b_(K-1) and\n\n    J=ceil(log(60 b_max/gamma)/log(3/2)).                  (14)\n\nThis can equivalently be selected by the finite integer test\n(3/2)^J>=60 b_max/gamma, with rational arithmetic when gamma is rational.\nIts finiteness follows from 3/2>1.\n\nHere is a common error bound with no unproved rates. Since\nsqrt(2)>5/4, lambda>9/4 and sqrt(lambda)>3/2. Also sqrt(2)<3/2,\nand (4) gives rho-1<1 and rho/2<1. For b>=1,\nj>=0, and q=(2/3)^j,\n\n    E(b,j)+2lambda^(-j/2)\n       <[12b+(3/25)(b+1)+9/10000+2]q\n       <=[12+6/25+9/10000+2]b q\n       <15b q.                                          (15)\n\nEvery inequality uses nonnegative terms; 2^(-j)<=q and\nlambda^(-j)<=q as well. Thus for all i and all j>=J,\n\n    E(b_i,j)+2u_j<gamma/4,   u_j=lambda^(-j/2).            (16)\n\nBy (2) and Z_b_i>=1,\n\n    B_(n_(i,j))>=lambda^j Z_b_i(1-E(b_i,j)).\n\nAlso (4) implies B_(n_(i,j))>=lambda^j, so\n\n    (1-A^(-1/2))/sqrt(B_(n_(i,j)))<=u_j.\n\nUsing (5), monotonicity, and the LOWER ray enclosure for the larger ray,\n\n    B_(N_(i,j))<=B_(m b_i 2^j-1)<=lambda^j Z_(m b_i),\n\nwe get, whenever (16) holds,\n\n    B_(N_(i,j))W_(N_(i,j))(H_(i,j))\n       <=[Z_(m b_i)/(A Z_b_i)]\n          /[(1-E(b_i,j))(1-u_j)^2].                      (17)\n\nThe factors in the denominator are positive by (16). For 0<=E,u<1,\n\n    (1-E)(1-u)^2\n       =1-E-2u+2Eu+(1-E)u^2>=1-E-2u.\n\nHence that denominator is greater than 1-gamma/4. For the fixed index\nselected by (13), Z_(m b_i)/(A Z_b_i)<=q_i(a)<1-gamma/2, so\n\n    B_(N_(i,j))W_(N_(i,j))(H_(i,j))\n       <(1-gamma/2)/(1-gamma/4)\n       <1-gamma/4,            EVERY j>=J.                (18)\n\nThe last strict inequality follows from\n(1-gamma/4)^2-(1-gamma/2)=gamma^2/16>0. Thus the explicit positive\nrelative separation is gamma/4, and the chosen phase is fixed before\nthe unbounded horizon sequence is used. The family and selection depend\nonly on the seed and benchmark, never on an objective or its trajectory.\n\n## 7. The exponent interface follows from a finite integer cover\n\nTake b0=d=1 and C_pc=1. Then (7) becomes precisely\n\n    product_(i=0)^(K-1) Z_(m^(i+1))/Z_(m^i)<=lambda^ell\n       whenever m^K<=2^ell.                              (19)\n\nThus A^K>lambda^ell is sufficient. This finite condition for some\nintegers K>=1,ell>=0 is equivalent to A>m^rho. In one direction,\nlambda^ell=(2^ell)^rho>=m^(K rho), so the strict power inequality implies\nA>m^rho. Conversely, if A>m^rho, choose an integer K with\n\n    K log(A/m^rho)>log(lambda)\n\nand set ell=ceil(K log_2(m)). Then m^K<=2^ell<2m^K, and\n\n    lambda^ell<lambda m^(K rho)<A^K.                     (20)\n\nHere rho>0 and lambda=2^rho justify raising inequalities to rho.\nIf desired first choose a rational a with m^rho<a<A and perform the\nsame argument with a; Sections 4--6 then apply with certified inputs.\nThis proves sufficiency of A>(r+1)^rho without a claim about an\nexponent obstruction or capacity ceiling for arbitrary seeds.\n\nFor an accepted upper comparison Z_d/Z_b0<=C_pc, the stronger finite\ninterface available from (7) is\n\n    A>(lambda^ell C_pc)^(1/K),\n    m^K b0<=2^ell d.                                    (21)\n\nThe word \"stronger\" refers to using this additional certified comparison;\nit is not an assertion that every choice in (21) beats (19), or that\nits value is below m^rho. For instance, at K=1,ell=0, b0=3 and d=3m,\nthe accepted constants in `4c92d3fc4eb6153e` recover its sufficient\ncapacity hypotheses for r=5 and r=6. Its more specialized horizon and\nmargin estimates remain valid in their stated scope.\n\n## 8. Exact rational examples, with no evaluator\n\nAll checks here are written as explicit integer equalities or positive\ninteger differences. They are mathematical parts of the joint proof,\nnot reports of computations executed by a program.\n\nFirst record small power identities:\n\n    lambda^4=17+12sqrt(2),\n    lambda^5=41+29sqrt(2),\n    lambda^10=3363+2378sqrt(2).\n\nThe last conjugate is lambda^(-10)>0, so\n\n    lambda^10<lambda^10+lambda^(-10)=6726<6750.            (22)\n\nAlso sqrt(2)<17/12 and sqrt(2)<99/70, because respectively\n289>288 and 9801>9800. Hence\n\n    lambda<29/12,  lambda<169/70,  lambda^4<34.            (23)\n\n### 8.1 Length five: capacity 49/5 and seventeen phases\n\nLet m=6, a=49/5, K=17, ell=44, b0=d=1, C_pc=1. The length cover is\n\n    6^17<=2^44\n      iff 3^17<=2^27,\n    3^17=129140163<134217728=2^27.                        (24)\n\nThe capacity power bound follows from small factored checks. First\n\n    49^4-9220*5^4=5764801-5762500=2301>0,\n\nso a^4>9220. Next\n\n    922^2=850084,  675^2=455625,\n    200*850084-373*455625\n      =170016800-169948125=68675>0,\n    49*373^2-170*200^2\n      =6817321-6800000=17321>0.                          (25)\n\nConsequently\n\n    lambda^44/a^17\n       <[34*6750^4]/[(49/5)*9220^4]\n       =170*675^4/(49*922^4)\n       <6800000/6817321<1.                              (26)\n\nThis proves the needed exact finite power inequality; no decimal\napproximation to rho is used. More quantitatively,\n\n    17321*10000=173210000>115894457=17*6817321,\n\nso (8) holds with gamma=1/10000, even at the capacity floor a=49/5.\nEvery actual full seed with r=5 and A>=49/5 therefore has a phase in\n\n    b_i=6^i,             0<=i<=16,\n    N_(i,j)=6^(i+1)2^j-6,\n\nwhich the certified procedure selects. With\n\n    J5=ceil(log(600000*6^16)/log(3/2)),\n\nits physical words satisfy, for EVERY j>=J5,\n\n    W_(N_(i,j))(H_(i,j))<(1-1/40000) U_(N_(i,j))^ZJ.     (27)\n\nThe capacity 49/5 is below 99/10 by exactly 1/10.\n\n### 8.2 Length six: capacity 12 and eleven phases\n\nLet m=7, a=12, K=11, ell=31, b0=d=1, C_pc=1. The exact length cover is\n\n    7^11=1977326743<2147483648=2^31.                     (28)\n\nUse (22)--(23) and the equality 6750=(125/32)12^3. Then\n\n    lambda^31/12^11\n       <6750^3*(169/70)/12^11\n       =125^3*169/(32^3*70*12^2)\n       =330078125/330301440<1,                          (29)\n\nsince the denominator minus the numerator is 223315. Furthermore\n\n    223315*20000=4466300000>3633315840=11*330301440.\n\nThus (8) holds with gamma=1/20000. Every actual full seed with r=6\nand A>=12 has a certified selectable phase in\n\n    b_i=7^i,             0<=i<=10,\n    N_(i,j)=7^(i+1)2^j-7.\n\nWith J6=ceil(log(1200000*7^10)/log(3/2)), for EVERY j>=J6 it gives\n\n    W_(N_(i,j))(H_(i,j))<(1-1/80000) U_(N_(i,j))^ZJ.     (30)\n\nThe capacity 12 is below 1201/100 by exactly 1/100.\n\n### 8.3 An accepted comparison shortens the length-five list\n\nFor an additional finite illustration, take m=6, a=197/20, K=9,\nell=21, b0=3, d=15, and C_pc=19299/2500. The accepted comparison in\n`04219554e41d9750` is Z_15/Z_3<C_pc. The cover reduces to\n\n    6^9*3<=2^21*15\n      iff 3^9<=5*2^12,\n    19683<20480.                                        (31)\n\nThe integer checks\n\n    197^3-950*20^3=7645373-7600000=45373>0,\n    4*19299=77196<77500=31*2500\n\ngive a^3>950 and C_pc<31/4. With (22)--(23),\n\n    lambda^21*C_pc/a^9\n      <[6750^2*(29/12)*(31/4)]/950^3\n       =899*135^2/(48*50*19^3)\n       =16384275/16461600\n       =218457/219488<1.                               (32)\n\nHere 135^2=18225, 19^3=6859, and\n16461600-16384275=77325. Moreover\n\n    1031*2000=2062000>1975392=9*219488.\n\nThus gamma=1/2000 satisfies (8). There are now only nine phases,\n\n    b_i=3*6^i,          0<=i<=8,\n    N_(i,j)=18*6^i*2^j-6.\n\nWith J5a=ceil(log(360000*6^8)/log(3/2)), the selected phase gives\nfor EVERY j>=J5a the relative separation 1/8000. The required capacity\n197/20 is below 99/10 by 1/20, but is above the smaller 49/5 capacity\nin Section 8.1. These are different finite tradeoffs, not an ordering\nof their unknown best true phases.\n\nFor this SAME K=9, the least unanchored dyadic exponent is 24, since\n\n    2^23=8388608<10077696=6^9<16777216=2^24.\n\nThe product bound lambda^21*C_pc is strictly smaller than lambda^24:\nC_pc<31/4<14<lambda^3, where lambda^3=7+5sqrt(2)>14 follows from\nsqrt(2)>7/5. This is a proved improvement over the unanchored finite\nbound at this fixed K. It asserts no optimality over all finite covers.\n\n## 9. Complete conditional theorem proved by the joint argument\n\nFix the original function class and ALL-split benchmark from Section 1.\nSuppose an actual length-r seed, r>=1, satisfies EVERY condition (1),\nwith h>=0 and no coordinate identifications, and put m=r+1, A=1+sum h.\nLet b0,d,K be positive integers and ell>=0 an integer. Let C_pc>0 be\na proved upper bound for Z_d/Z_b0 and assume\n\n    m^K b0<=2^ell d,    A^K>lambda^ell C_pc.\n\nChoose any certified floor 1<a<=A and gamma>0 satisfying\n\n    a^K>lambda^ell C_pc,\n    K gamma<=1-lambda^ell C_pc/a^K.\n\nSuch real choices exist, and rational choices exist under the same strict\ninequality, as explained in Section 6. Write P_tau for the orthogonal\nprojection onto the vectors supported on tau whose three coordinates sum\nto zero. The sum of the three unoriented edge outer products on tau is\n3P_tau. Every unordered edge occurs in N-2 triangles, while\nsum_(u<v)(e_u-e_v)(e_u-e_v)^T=N P_N: its diagonal entries are N-1 and\nits off-diagonal entries are -1. Consequently\n\n sum_tau P_tau = N(N-2)P_N/3,\n sum_tau w_tri P_tau=P_N.                                (4)\n\nLet A_tri have one row sqrt(w_tri/3)*(e_u-e_v)^T for every separately\nindexed directed edge u->v in every triangle. Then\n\n A_tri^T A_tri=P_N,\n F_N(x)=|| (A_tri x)_+ ||^2/2,\n grad F_N(x)=A_tri^T (A_tri x)_+.                         (5)\n\nIn particular A_tri is an isometry on E_N and has operator norm1 on R^N.\nIts range projection is Pi_tri=A_tri A_tri^T: indeed Pi_tri is symmetric,\nand Pi_tri^2=A_tri P_N A_tri^T=Pi_tri.\n\nEach scalar function t_+^2/2 is convex and continuously differentiable,\nwith derivative t_+. Thus F_N is convex and differentiable. Since the\ncomponentwise positive-part map is 1-Lipschitz, (5) gives\n\n ||grad F_N(x)-grad F_N(y)|| <= ||x-y||.\n\nHence F_N is an everywhere-defined convex 1-smooth function. No assertion\nthat this smoothness upper bound is the least possible constant for every\norientation and N is needed or made. The normalization in (3) is fixed.\n\n## 4. Every directed row, the minimum, physical GD and true distance\n\nFor arbitrary real t,u direct consideration of their four sign pairs gives\n\n u_+^2/2-t_+^2/2-t_+*(u-t)\n       =(u_+-t_+)^2/2+t_+*(-u)_+.                        (6)\n\nFor x,y put r=(A_tri x)_+, s=(A_tri y)_+, d=r-s. Summing (6), and using\ngrad F_N(x)=A_tri^T r, gives\n\n F_N(y)-F_N(x)-<grad F_N(x),y-x>\n       =||d||^2/2+sum_e r_e*(-(A_tri y)_e)_+.\n\nBecause Pi_tri is the range projection,\n||A_tri^T d||^2=||Pi_tri d||^2 and\n||d||^2=||Pi_tri d||^2+||(I-Pi_tri)d||^2. Therefore the exact residual is\n\n Q(x,y):=F_N(x)-F_N(y)+<grad F_N(x),y-x>\n                       +||grad F_N(x)-grad F_N(y)||^2/2\n =-sum_e (A_tri x)_+,e*(-(A_tri y)_e)_+\n  -||(I-Pi_tri)((A_tri x)_+-(A_tri y)_+)||^2/2 <=0.        (8)\n\nThe orientation here agrees exactly with (2). It holds for EVERY x,y,\nso all ordered original trajectory pairs and every nonlocal cycle pass.\nIt includes equal points at zero steps and both directions involving any\nminimizer. No finite collection of adjacent checks is substituted for (8).\n\nClearly F_N>=0. Equality forces every directed difference in every triangle\nto be nonpositive. Around a directed triangle the three differences sum\nto zero, so all three must be zero. Every two vertices occur in some\ntriangle; all coordinates are therefore equal. Conversely constant\nvectors give value0. Hence\n\n argmin F_N=span{1}, min F_N=0,\n x_star=(sum_u x_0,u/N)*1,\n R_tri=dist(x_0,argmin F_N)=||P_N x_0||.                  (9)\n\nWe always take x_0 outside the minimum set, so R_tri>0. The mean coordinate\nis unchanged by GD because every edge vector has coordinate sum0.\n\nFor ANY finite nonnegative word h=(h_0,...,h_(n-1)), including zero steps,\nthe exact physical recursion is\n\n g_i=(w_tri/3)*sum_tau sum_(u->v in E_tau)\n                    (x_i,u-x_i,v)_+*(e_u-e_v),\n x_(i+1)=x_i-h_i*g_i, 0<=i<n,\n f_i=F_N(x_i), 0<=i<=n.                                 (10)\n\nThere is no compressed or restarted child state. It is permissible to\ncompute g_n, although it is not used in the recursion. The exact actual\nterminal payoff is\n\n V_tri(h,x_0)=2F_N(x_n)/R_tri^2\n   =[w_tri/(3R_tri^2)]*sum_tau sum_(u->v in E_tau)\n                                      (x_n,u-x_n,v)_+^2. (11)\n\nOne explicit unit-distance start for every N is\nv_N=sqrt(N/(N-1))*(e_0-(1/N)*1). Exact triangle radial bounds and its sharp one-step norm factor\n\nFirst work on one triangle's mean-zero plane, with\nf_triangle(z)=[(z_0-z_1)_+^2+(z_1-z_2)_+^2+(z_2-z_0)_+^2]/6.\nFor an oriented triangle tau, f_tau denotes this same sum-of-three-edges\nformula on the plane range(P_tau), with that triangle's vertex labels.\nReversing the cyclic orientation is obtained by replacing z by -z,\nso the following bounds hold for either orientation.\n\nThere are two sector types, with their boundaries allowed. In a two-positive\nsector, after a cyclic relabelling, let the positive successive gaps be\nu=z_0-z_1>=0 and v=z_1-z_2>=0. The centered coordinates give\n\n ||z||^2=2(u^2+uv+v^2)/3,\n 2f_triangle(z)=(u^2+v^2)/3.\n\nIn a one-positive sector put p=z_0-z_1>0 and let\ns=z_2-z_1 in [0,p], so the other differences are -s and -(p-s). (18)\n\nFor a nonnegative step t define the piecewise scalar\n\n q_tri(t)=1-t/3,                         0<=t<=3/2;\n          sqrt(1-t+t^2/3),               3/2<=t<=3;\n          2t/3-1,                       t>=3.
